'''Thomas Rivera Schatz''' (born June 10, 1966), also known by his initials '''TRS''', is a [[Puerto Ricans|Puerto Rican]] [[politician]], legal advisor, [[Attorney at law|attorney]], and former [[prosecutor|prosecutor, who was the]] fourteenth, sixteenth and is currently the eighteenth [[President of the Senate of Puerto Rico]]. He is affiliated with [[New Progressive Party of Puerto Rico]] (abbr. PNP in Spanish) and the USA's [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], in particular with the [[Log Cabin Republicans]].

His tenure as president of the senate has been marred with multiple scandals regarding [[no-show jobs|ghost employees]] on the payroll of his office,<ref >{{cite news |author=Primera Hora|date=13 September 2019|title=Federales citan a Thomas Rivera Schatz por caso de contratistas fantasmas en el Capitolio|url= https://www.primerahora.com/noticias/policia-tribunales/notas/federales-citan-a-thomas-rivera-schatz-por-caso-de-contratistas-fantasmas-en-el-capitolio/|trans-title=Federal authorities summon Thomas Rivera Schatz in Capitol Hill ghost contractors case|language=Spanish|work=Primera Hora|location=Guaynabo|access-date=14 March 2026}}</ref> and the conviction of several of his closest colleagues and subordinates on corruption charges, including [[Héctor Martínez Maldonado]], José Gómez Zaldo, Juan Carlos Acosta Ramírez, Alex Emille Martínez Morales, among others.<ref>{{cite news |author=Primera Hora|date=30 January 2012|title=Cabecilla de organización deja solo a ex empleado senatorial|url=https://www.primerahora.com/noticias/policia-tribunales/notas/cabecilla-de-organizacion-deja-solo-a-ex-empleado-senatorial/|trans-title=Organization leader leaves former Senate employee alone|language=Spanish|work=Primera Hora|location=Guaynabo|access-date=14 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=NotiCel|date=7 March 2025|title=Apelativo sostiene sentencias a convictos por corrupción en Superintendencia del Capitolio |url=https://noticel.com/ultima-hora/20250307/apelativo-sostiene-sentencias-a-convictos-por-corrupcion-en-superintendencia-del-capitolio/|trans-title=Appeals court upholds sentences for those convicted of corruption in the Capitol Superintendence|language=Spanish|work=NotiCel|location=San Juan|access-date=14 March 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and studies==
Rivera Schatz was born on June 10, 1966, in the [[Bronx|Bronx Borough]] of [[New York City]]. He is the son of [[José Rivera Díaz|José A. "Nía" Rivera]], a past mayor of [[Trujillo Alto, Puerto Rico|Trujillo Alto]], and Christina Schatz, a German woman.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/vocero.com/docs/v05132012/4|title=El Vocero de Puerto Rico|website=Issuu.com |date=13 May 2012 }}</ref> While in college, he worked full-time at the City of San Juan Public Works Department. He attended the [[Interamerican University of Puerto Rico School of Law]], where he graduated in 1992. A year later, he passed the [[bar exam]] required to practice law in Puerto Rico.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hon. THOMAS RIVERA SCHATZ |url=http://www.senadopr.us/senadores/HONTHOMASRIVERASCHATZ/Pages/default.aspx |access-date=18 June 2021 |date=2009-08-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090829203359/http://www.senadopr.us/senadores/HONTHOMASRIVERASCHATZ/Pages/default.aspx |archive-date=2009-08-29 }}</ref>

Rivera Schatz started his legal career as a legal advisor in the [[Senate of Puerto Rico|Senate]] and [[Puerto Rico House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] of Puerto Rico. In 1996, [[Governor]] [[Pedro Rosselló]] appointed him as a prosecutor at the [[Puerto Rico Department of Justice]]. After finishing his service as a prosecutor, he returned to private practice, handling both criminal and civil cases.

==Political career==
===Electoral Commissioner and Secretary General: 2000–2007===
In 2000, Rivera Schatz was named Electoral Commissioner for the pro-statehood [[New Progressive Party of Puerto Rico|New Progressive Party]] (PNP).

Two years later, party president [[Pedro Rosselló]] named Rivera Schatz as secretary general of the PNP in addition to his current position as electoral commissioner. He served both positions simultaneously until August 1, 2007, when he decided to run for senator.

During his tenure as PNP Secretary General, Rivera Schatz orchestrated the expulsion or suspension of five sitting PNP senators who had refused to support Pedro Rosselló's bid to unseat McClintock as Senate President, calling the dissenting senators "traitors". Rivera Schatz filed the party grievances, imposed sanctions without hearings or prior notice, and barred several of them from running under the PNP banner.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-11-13 |title=Historia de choques y de reencuentro |url=https://www.primerahora.com/noticias/gobierno-politica/notas/historia-de-choques-y-de-reencuentro/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Primera Hora |language=es}}</ref> The senators challenged the actions in court, and in 2007 the [https://dts.poderjudicial.pr/ts/2007/2007TSPR230.pdf Puerto Rico Supreme Court ruled 5-1 against Rivera Schatz and the PNP], finding that the party had violated both its own internal regulations and the Electoral Law's due process guarantees. This episode was not an isolated incident but an early and documented demonstration of the authoritarian political style that would define Rivera Schatz's career: using institutional mechanisms to silence dissent, punish disloyalty, and consolidate power — a pattern that would repeat itself, with greater reach and consequence, during his years as Senate President.

===.Senator: 2008–present===
Rivera Schatz ran for senator at the [[New Progressive Party primaries, 2008|PNP primaries]] where he won a slot in the ballot, receiving the second-most votes. In the [[Puerto Rican general election, 2008|2008 general elections]], Rivera Schatz was elected senator. His fellow senators then elected him to be the 14th president of Puerto Rico's Senate. As such, he selected the following persons for his team:
* Senator [[Margarita Nolasco]] as Senate President [[Pro tempore]]
* Senator [[Larry Seilhamer]] as majority leader
* Senator [[Melinda Romero]] as [[Majority Whip]]
* Roberto "Junior" Maldonado as chief administrative officer of the Senate.
* Senate Secretary [[Manuel A. Torres]] was nominated by Rivera Schatz and reelected to a second term, becoming the first Senate secretary to serve under two different Senate Presidents
* Incumbent Superintendent of the Capitol, Eliezer Velázquez, was nominated by Rivera Schatz and ratified by House Speaker [[Jenniffer González]] for a second term, a first for a superintendent.

Rivera Schatz was sworn into his post on January 12, 2009.

Thomas Rivera Schatz was reelected in 2012 and elected for the third time as a member of the Senate majority in the 2016 election with 10.33% of the "at large" votes, placing him in second place after independent senatorial candidate Dr. José Vargas Vidot and followed by Juan Dalmau of the Puerto Rico Independence Party (PIP).<ref>{{cite web |title=CEE Event |url=http://elecciones2016.ceepur.org/#es/pic_bar_list/SENADORES_POR_ACUMULACION_Resumen.xml |website= |access-date=18 June 2021 |date=2016-11-10 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20161110041719/http://elecciones2016.ceepur.org/#es/pic_bar_list/SENADORES_POR_ACUMULACION_Resumen.xml |archive-date=10 November 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Rivera Schatz was elected to a second term as President of the Senate of Puerto Rico starting January 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.univision.com/local/puerto-rico-wlii/thomas-rivera-schatz-regresa-a-la-presidencia-del-senado|title=Thomas Rivera Schatz regresa a la presidencia del Senado|website=Univision.com |date=9 November 2016 }}</ref>  He holds two records, first as the only reelected Senate President during the past 28 years and the only Senate President ever elected as such to non-consecutive terms. On November 5, 2024, he was elected President of the Senate for a third non-consecutive term.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/noticias/legislatura/notas/thomas-rivera-schatz-sera-el-nuevo-presidente-del-senado/|title=Thomas Rivera Schatz será el nuevo presidente del Senado|website=Elnuevodia.com |date=7 November 2024 }}</ref>

==PNP President==
On July 22, 2019, Rivera Schatz announced he would succeed Puerto Rican Governor Ricardo Rosselló as head of the [[New Progressive Party of Puerto Rico]] (PNP).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.primerahora.com/noticias/gobierno-politica/nota/thomasriveraschatzseautoproclamapresidentedelpnp-1354153/|title=Thomas Rivera Schatz se autoproclama presidente del PNP|date=July 22, 2019|website=Primera Hora}}</ref> Rosselló announced his intention to resign due to the ongoing controversy surrounding [[Telegramgate]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://nypost.com/2019/07/21/puerto-rico-governor-will-not-seek-reelection-amid-texting-scandal/|title=Puerto Rico governor will not seek reelection amid texting scandal|last=Tacopino|first=Joe|date=2019-07-21|newspaper=[[New York Post]]|language=en|access-date=2019-07-22}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Rivera Schatz and his father collect antique cars,<ref>[https://www.adendi.com/archivo.asp?Xnum=790701&year=2010&mon=10 Rivera Schatz "quema la fiebre" en Pennsylvania] on ''[[El Nuevo Día]]''; Rosario, Frances (October 2, 2010)</ref><ref>[http://www.vocero.com/noticias-es/detras-del-politico-2 Detras del político] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206120258/http://www.vocero.com/noticias-es/detras-del-politico-2 |date=2013-12-06 }} on ''[[El Vocero]]''; Méndez, Milly (February 11, 2011)</ref> and are fans of the New York Yankees. He is the father of 3 children, all born out of wedlock, one of which he has never publicly recognized and has physical disabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-06-06 |title=TRS: benévolo con un cuñado, pero implacable con el otro - NotiCel - La verdad como es - Noticias de Puerto Rico - NOTICEL |url=https://noticel.com/ultima-hora/20110606/trs-benevolo-con-un-cunado-pero-implacable-con-el-otro/ |access-date=2026-06-05 |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NotiCel™              - TRS tiene en nómina a su familia "no tradicional" |url=http://www.noticel.com:80/noticia/105468/trs-tiene-en-nomina-a-su-familia-no-tradicional.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605051850/http://www.noticel.com:80/noticia/105468/trs-tiene-en-nomina-a-su-familia-no-tradicional.html |archive-date=2011-06-05 |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=www.noticel.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NotiCel™              - Rivera Schatz y su familia "no tradicional" |url=http://www.noticel.com/noticia/105416/rivera-schatz-y-su-familia-no-tradicional.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604045646/http://www.noticel.com/noticia/105416/rivera-schatz-y-su-familia-no-tradicional.html |archive-date=2011-06-04 |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=www.noticel.com |language=en}}</ref>
